title: Stuck in a Chain? How Bridging Loans Work
summary: Educational blog article (not a case study). Thesis as revealed by the search excerpt: a bridging loan is a fast, short-term facility secured against property, typically 3 to 24 months, used to bridge the liquidity shortage that arises when a property chain breaks, i.e. when there is a lag between the cash flow from selling one property and the money needed to buy another. Concrete guidance surfaced: before borrowing, (1) pin down the timing gap, (2) choose the security, (3) set an exit strategy, which the article says is often the part of the deal the lender is most concerned about. Search (b) summarised the article together with eight other Silver Oak bridging pages and attributed to the site as a whole: bridging finance keeps a purchase moving while another sale is delayed; rates are higher than a standard mortgage; most products are interest-only with interest paid monthly or rolled up; repayment is usually via sale of the property or refinancing into a long-term mortgage; approvals advertised in 5-14 days with funds usually released within days or weeks; lenders look at property value, exit plan and speed. These [b] points cannot be reliably attributed to this specific article. The full article body, its H1, meta description, FAQ, fees, calls to action and any worked example were NOT returned by either search.
verbatim: [a] A bridging loan is a fast, short-term facility (typically between 3 and 24 months) secured against property.
[a][b] This gap is often referred to as a "broken chain" where there exists a liquidity shortage due to a lag in the timeline of cash flow between selling and buying property.

[a] (search-tool paraphrase of the article, not a quoted sentence) It recommends pinning down the timing gap, choosing the security, and setting an exit strategy. It notes the exit strategy is often the part of a deal the lender is most concerned about.
[b] (search-tool paraphrase, attributed to 'the same guide' i.e. this article) bridging finance is pitched as a way to keep a purchase moving while another sale is delayed.
[b] (site-wide summary, page not identified) typical term of between 3 and 24 months, secured against property. Another gives usually between 6 to 24 months.
[b] (site-wide summary, page not identified) The firm advertises approvals in 5–14 days, and says funds are usually released within days or weeks.
[b] (explicitly 'a related page', not this article) lenders may ask for the income/wealth is verified by a UK solicitor or accountant before completing.
